description:
Issue summary
Aurora Search is reporting that Structured Output (JSON-schema / strict schema validation) returns validation errors that are hard to interpret and sometimes inconsistent across request types (streaming vs non-streaming) and SDKs. Errors frequently lack:
- Which field/path failed validation
- Whether the failure is due to schema shape vs model output vs response_format configuration
- A copy/paste-ready example of a valid output for the given schema

Customer impact
- Increased time-to-triage for what should be a simple client-side fix
- Multiple repeat tickets from different engineers on the same team (same symptom, different prompts)
- Customers are turning off structured output or adding brittle post-processing, increasing failure rate and Support volume

Customer request
1) Improve error message clarity (field path + constraint + example)
2) Docs: add a troubleshooting section + guidance on common mistakes (arrays vs objects, required fields, enums, additionalProperties)
3) SDKs: ensure the error surfaces request_id and a stable error code that Support can search

Environment
- Hosted API (prod), regions observed: us-east + eu-west
- Models: redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct and redwood/qwen2.5-32b-instruct
- Customer reports the issue in both Python SDK and TypeScript SDK; we reproduced with raw HTTP as well

What the customer sees (anonymized)
A) Non-streaming request returns 400 with vague message
- HTTP 400
- message: "Structured output validation failed" (no field path)
- sometimes includes: "schema invalid" even when schema is accepted on other calls

B) Streaming request fails mid-stream with an SSE error event that does not contain validation details
- stream ends with an error
- customer cannot tell whether partial output was invalid JSON, missing required keys, wrong types, etc.

Example schema (customer-provided, lightly anonymized)
- Object with required fields: {"id": string, "confidence": number, "tags": array<string>}
- Customer reports that if the model returns confidence as a quoted string ("0.82"), the error does not indicate which field is wrong

Support reproduction (internal)
- Using curl against /v1/chat/completions with response_format set to JSON schema.
- When forcing the model to return an invalid type for a required field, we see a generic validation error without a pointer (e.g., "confidence") and without the offending value.

Expected
- Error response should include:
  - Stable error code (e.g., structured_output.validation_failed)
  - request_id (already in headers; ensure included/propagated in SDK exceptions)
  - JSON pointer / field path (e.g., $.confidence)
  - Expected type/constraint + actual type (e.g., expected number, got string)
  - Actionable guidance ("return a number, not a quoted string")

Notes / constraints
- Do not include customer prompts verbatim in broadly visible docs.
- If we include snippets, use short, generic examples and clearly label them.
- Ensure error payload is safe to log (avoid echoing full model output; consider truncation and redaction).

Ask / next steps
- Eng: confirm current validation layer (gateway vs runtime) and what details are available to surface safely.
- Docs/DevEx: draft a structured output troubleshooting page + add to known-issues index if we want Support deflection.
- Support: add a macro for "Structured output validation" that requests schema + minimal failing output + request_id and links to docs once published.
comments: 2026-02-20 (Priya Shah): Customer reports repeated confusion with structured output errors. They are getting "validation failed" without the failing field. Asked for 3 request_ids and their response_format payload (schema only, no prompt).
2026-02-20 (Owen Phillips): Confirmed we should treat as P2/Sev3 (no platform outage). Tagging as deflection candidate for known-issues sprint. Added to Support macro refresh list.

2026-02-21 (Customer - Aurora Search, via Support email): Provided request_ids: rwreq_01HSO8V7Y3QK2..., rwreq_01HSO8W1N9J0A..., rwreq_01HSO8W6TQ0F7... (full IDs in private note). Reports both Python 1.18.2 and TS 0.9.4. Says error is "schema invalid" on some calls, "validation failed" on others for same schema.

2026-02-21 (Owen Phillips): Reproduced with curl using an internal test prompt. Observed response is 400 with generic message; no JSON path. In streaming mode, error arrives as SSE event "error" with message only. Looping in Platform for error payload consistency guidance.

2026-02-22 (Ethan Park): Took a look. We currently collapse validator errors to a single message at the API boundary to avoid leaking output. We should be able to safely include JSON pointer + expected/actual types without including full output. Agree this is a gap. Suggest creating a small structured error object and truncating any sample value to N chars if we include it.

2026-02-22 (Wei Chen): From docs side: we don’t have a dedicated troubleshooting section for structured output beyond the basic guide. I can draft a short page with common failures (required fields, enums, type mismatches, additionalProperties) and recommended prompt patterns. Need final error codes/payload shape to document.

2026-02-23 (Owen Phillips): Created follow-up items in Linear: ENG-4861 (error payload improvements) + ENG-4862 (docs troubleshooting). Will keep this ticket open until we have (1) committed plan + (2) published docs link we can use in macros.

2026-02-25 (Mina Haddad): One nuance: fallback routing can change model family; structured output adherence differs by model. We should make sure docs mention pinning models + using stricter prompts for smaller models. Not suggesting that we blame the model; just set expectations and provide mitigations.

2026-02-28 (Owen Phillips): Proposed customer-facing interim guidance (until errors improve): recommend including an explicit example JSON in the prompt and instructing "do not quote numbers" / "output must exactly match schema"; also suggest testing in non-stream mode to capture full error response for now. Pending Eng confirmation if any near-term patch can add JSON path to the error message.
resolution: Unresolved. Tracking improvements via Linear ENG-4861 (add JSON path + expected/actual types + stable error code; ensure request_id propagation) and ENG-4862 (publish structured output troubleshooting docs and link from known-issues index + Support macros). Interim workaround sent to customer: add explicit example output; avoid streaming while debugging; capture request_id + schema for Support.
